review_notes: I read the whole file and looked for declarations that introduce a concept Mathlib already has. I did not open the other project files or search Mathlib, so this rests on the file text alone. The file defines only a few new objects. The private helpers `normalizedRightDual`, `normalizedRightDualFP`, `normalizedRightDualCongr`, `canonicalDualClassValue`, `canonicalDualClassHom` and `doubleDualExtensionEquiv` are thin compositions of existing pieces. Those pieces are `ModuleCat.restrictScalars`, `ModuleCat.rightDual`, `LinearEquiv.congrLeft`, `LinearMap.coprodEquiv`, `LinearMap.bidualEvalEquiv` and `ProjectiveClass.lift`. The public `ProjectiveClass.dualEquiv` and `K0.dualEquiv` are an equivalence between the classes of finite projective modules of `R` and `Rᵐᵒᵖ`, and between the K₀ groups. These are new mathematical content and not duplicates of anything in Mathlib. `K0.dualEquiv` is built from Mathlib's `AddSubmonoid.LocalizationMap.addEquivOfAddEquiv`, and the inverse completion square uses `addEquivOfLocalizations` and `ofAddEquivOfDom`, so it reuses the stock localization API. The `RightExtension` scalar-extension API that this file uses is defined in other project files. I did not review those files, and they are outside this target. The file adds no competing duplicate of a Mathlib concept that I could justify.
